title: SYSK Selects: How Immigration Works
summary: SYSK Selects episode, a rerun of the classic episode on how immigration works. Josh introduces it as a selection and the hosts open with news that the DREAM Act passed the House. The main content covers Ellis Island history, legal immigration terminology (immigrant vs. emigrant, alien types, lawful permanent resident, naturalization), the agencies involved (INS, DHS, USCIS, Customs and Border Protection, State Department), family-based, employment-based, diversity lottery and investor visas, asylum (affirmative and defensive, expedited removal), refugees, illegal immigration and the guest worker debate, amnesty history, and a closing listener mail segment for a birthday shout-out.

segments.title: Selects intro and DREAM Act news
segments.summary: Josh introduces this week's SYSK Selects pick, the classic How Immigration Works. The hosts banter about the podcast's ranking and social media, then discuss the DREAM Act passing the House and its path to citizenship for certain children brought to the US illegally.

segments.title: Ellis Island and immigration history
segments.summary: The hosts describe Ellis Island's history as a immigration station from 1892 to 1954, through which about twelve million immigrants passed, and note that many Americans have immigrant ancestors. They also distinguish nativists from Native Americans.

segments.title: Naturalization ceremonies
segments.summary: Chuck recounts working on a documentary about Jane Seymour's naturalization and attending a naturalization ceremony in Los Angeles, describing the emotion of the event.

segments.title: Immigration vs. emigration and government agencies
segments.summary: The hosts explain immigrate versus emigrate and list the agencies involved: the former INS, now under Department of Homeland Security, with Customs and Border Protection and USCIS. Congress writes immigration law while the president influences refugee policy.

segments.title: Types of aliens and lawful permanent residents
segments.summary: The hosts define alien terms, including resident alien, nonresident alien, and naturalized citizen, and describe lawful permanent residents, who can live and work in the US but cannot vote or serve on juries.

segments.title: Visas and family-based immigration
segments.summary: The hosts walk through applying for an immigrant visa at a consulate, the port of entry inspection, and the affidavit of support requirement at the poverty line. They cover family preference categories, from immediate relatives of citizens through fourth-preference siblings of adult citizens.

segments.title: Diversity lottery, employment and investor visas
segments.summary: The hosts describe the diversity visa lottery with about 50,000 visas a year from countries with low US immigration. They cover employment-based categories EB-1 through EB-4, labor certification, and investor visas requiring investment and job creation, including the regional center pilot program.

segments.title: Immigration maps
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck briefly mention cartogram maps showing immigration and refugee flows.

segments.title: Asylum, affirmative and defensive
segments.summary: The hosts explain asylum for people with a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or social group. They distinguish affirmative asylum, filed within a year of arrival in a non-adversarial interview, from defensive asylum in court, and describe expedited removal and the four screening questions.

segments.title: Refugees
segments.summary: The hosts note worldwide refugee numbers of about 13.6 million, that the US admitted about 60,000 refugees in the most recent year, and that Canada was next. They agree to cover refugees in a future episode.

segments.title: Illegal immigration, guest workers, and amnesty
segments.summary: The hosts discuss illegal immigration controversy, estimated illegal population of 10.8 million, border violence in Mexico, coyotes and drug smuggling, the guest worker proposal, the Bracero Program, Operation Wetback, and past amnesties including the Mariel boatlift, Central American Relief Act, and the 1986 Immigration Reform and Control Act signed by Reagan. They also mention the border fence and the Minutemen.

segments.title: Listener mail: birthday shout-out for Elona
segments.summary: Listener Eric asks for a birthday shout-out to his friend Elona, saying he has collected messages from musicians for her. The hosts agree to do a happy birthday segment and ask listeners to email their shout-outs.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: The hosts close with a pointer to HowStuffWorks.com for more on immigration and information about the podcast and iPhone app.
